subject: Oceanography
title: Mangrove Coasts
description: A quick, practical guide to Mangrove Coasts.

hook.text: Mangroves stand in saltwater on stilt-like roots—building land where waves would normally erode it.

buildup.text: Their tangled roots trap sediment from the water, gradually extending the coastline seaward.

discovery.text: Mangrove forests reduce wave energy by up to 66%—acting as natural breakwaters for coastal communities.

twist.text: They also serve as nurseries for commercial fish species—75% of tropical fish spend time in mangroves.

climax.text: Yet half the world's mangroves have been destroyed—cleared for shrimp farms, ports, and development.

punchline.text: Trees that walk on water protect entire coastlines.

quiz.question: How do mangroves protect coasts?
options: They trap sediment and reduce wave energy
